patches.fact: Line from Lake of the Angels to the west-ridge notch
patches.find: climb roughly 800 ft up onto the ROCK RIB above the lake's basin and CROSS TO ITS NORTH SIDE. A rib is a shape underfoot — the ground rises to a spine and falls away on both sides — so it is identifiable in cloud, and the instruction to cross to the far side of it is a check you can perform without seeing anything. SECOND TEST: from the north side of the rib, Class 2-3 terrain leads up
patches.replace: a boot path climbs a couple of hundred feet toward ST. PETER'S GATE, and SHORT OF THE GATE you turn LEFT along the BASE OF THE LONG CLIFF BAND. Rock wall at your shoulder on one side and scree dropping away on the other is a check you can make in cloud without seeing anything further. SECOND TEST: along the cliff base, Class 2-3 ground and a couple of narrow chutes lead up

results.fact: Which top is the true summit
results.correct_value: The south summit (~6,280 ft) is the true high point; the north summit (~6,212 ft) is lower.
results.evidence: A regional hiking guide states the 6,280 ft south summit is the mountain's highest point, reached 0.1 mi off a junction at 4.0 mi, with the northern summit at 6,212 ft; a 2024 trip report gives Mt. Townsend 6,280 ft and North Mt. Townsend 6,211 ft down the ridge. So there is no higher point beyond the south summit; overview, pro_tips and the itinerary wrongly called the south summit a mere viewpoint.
